Q7.note: Unlike Kafka, KoP keeps reading a connection while earlier requests are pending (up to maxQueuedRequests = 500, responses in order), so several fetches can wait at once, each completed by a produce to its partition. Q4.note: The request's enqueue time is not sent. The long-poll response does carry lacUpdateTimestamp: the bookie's wall-clock ms when the LAC advanced past the request's previousLAC while the request waited (absent if it did not wait). Q7.note: The segment store parks a read at or beyond the end of an open segment until data reaches its offset, handles reads asynchronously, and matches replies by requestId, so a consumer can keep several reads waiting at successive offsets, each completed by the data that reaches its offset. Reads name byte offsets, so this keeps a read waiting for each next event only when event sizes are known (e.g. fixed-size events). The reader-group client itself keeps one outstanding read per segment.
